group.passage: Today it is hard to picture an airport without rolling luggage. Yet carts and wagons have rolled along roads for thousands of years, while bags on wheels are a fairly recent idea. Below, a short history of the invention is followed by a travel writer’s column on why it arrived so late.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: How Luggage Learned to Roll
passage_parts.text: People tried putting wheels on luggage long before the idea caught on. Patents were issued for a wheeled trunk in 1887 and for a wheeled suitcase in 1945, but neither attracted many buyers. The real turning point came in 1970. Bernard Sadow, an executive at a luggage company, was struggling with two heavy suitcases at an airport in Puerto Rico when he watched a worker push a heavy machine along on a small platform with wheels. Back home, he fixed four small wheels under a suitcase and attached a strap so that it could be towed like a dog on a leash. Department stores in New York turned him down, insisting that nobody would ever pull a bag behind them, until Macy’s agreed to give it a try. Still, his design was far from perfect. In 1987, an airline pilot named Robert Plath stood the bag on its end, put two wheels at the bottom, and added a long handle that slides back inside. Pilots and flight attendants were quick to adopt it, and ordinary travelers soon followed.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Travel Column: The Bag That Came Late
passage_parts.text: Whenever I watch travelers glide through an airport, I wonder why it took so long for anyone to put wheels on a suitcase. The technology was hardly the problem. My guess is that, for most of history, people seldom had to carry their own bags very far. Porters waited at every train station and hotel, happy to take your luggage for a small tip. Things changed when the number of people flying grew rapidly and airports became huge, leaving passengers to haul their belongings down endless corridors by themselves. Pride may have played a part as well. My grandfather, who traveled constantly for work, thought rolling bags looked silly and carried his heavy case by hand until his back finally made him give in. Perhaps we simply stop noticing a problem once it becomes part of everyday life. Every time I roll my bag onto a train, I am grateful that somebody finally thought of it.

1.strategy_zh: 先看結構：was ___ by airline crews 是被動語態，空格要過去分詞。再想 airline crews（機組人員）在 Text A 換成了哪些字（pilots and flight attendants），找到他們對這個新設計「做了什麼」。

airline crews 就是 Text A 最後一句的 pilots and flight attendants，他們對 Plath 的新行李箱做了什麼？

2.explanation_zh: Text B 的專欄作者認為，以前大多有搬運工代勞，旅客很少需要自己提行李走遠路；直到搭飛機的人數快速成長（grew rapidly）、機場變得很大，旅客只好自己拖著行李走長長的走廊，輪子才變得有必要。摘要句 until the ___ of air travel 中，空格在冠詞 the 之後、介系詞 of 之前，要填名詞，所以把動詞 grow（文中是過去式 grew）轉成名詞 growth（成長）。
evidence: Things changed when the number of people flying grew rapidly and airports became huge, leaving passengers to haul their belongings down endless corridors by themselves.
2.strategy_zh: the ___ of air travel：空格前有 the、後有 of，一定是名詞。再到 Text B 找「情況改變」（Things changed）的那一句，看搭飛機的人數怎麼了，把那個動詞改成名詞。
hints: the ___ of air travel：空格要填名詞。
在 Text B 找 Things changed 那一句：搭飛機的人數發生了什麼變化？

Bernard Sadow, an executive at a luggage company, was struggling with two heavy suitcases at an airport in Puerto Rico when he watched a worker push a heavy machine along on a small platform with wheels.

3.strategy_zh: 「兩篇都符合」題：每個選項都要在 Text A、Text B 各找到一句根據才選。只在一篇成立、兩篇都沒提到，或乍看符合大意卻被其中一篇的細節（例如年份）推翻的選項都不能選；不確定的寧可不選，避免倒扣。

translation_zh.text:
今天，很難想像機場裡沒有滾輪行李。然而，手推車和馬車在路上滾動已經有幾千年了，裝了輪子的袋子卻是相當晚近的點子。以下先是一篇關於這項發明的簡史，接著是一位旅遊作家的專欄，談它為什麼這麼晚才出現。

Text A（行李如何學會滾動）
早在這個點子流行起來之前，人們就試過在行李上裝輪子。1887 年就有附輪子的大皮箱取得了專利，1945 年也有附輪子的行李箱取得專利，但兩者都沒吸引到多少買家。真正的轉捩點出現在 1970 年。行李公司主管 Bernard Sadow 在波多黎各的機場吃力地搬著兩個沉重的行李箱時，看到一名工人把一台沉重的機器放在裝了輪子的小平台上推著走。回家後，他在行李箱底部裝了四個小輪子，再繫上一條帶子，好讓行李箱能像用牽繩遛狗一樣被拖著走。紐約的百貨公司都拒絕了他，堅稱沒有人會拖著袋子走在後面，直到梅西百貨同意試賣。不過，他的設計還遠稱不上完美。1987 年，一位名叫 Robert Plath 的航空公司機師把行李箱立起來，在底部裝上兩個輪子，再加上一根可以滑回箱內的長拉桿。機師和空服員很快就採用了它，一般旅客不久也跟進。

Text B（旅遊專欄：來得很晚的行李箱）
每當我看著旅客在機場裡輕快地滑行而過，我都會納悶：為什麼過了那麼久才有人在行李箱上裝輪子？技術幾乎不是問題。我猜，在歷史上大部分的時間裡，人們很少需要自己把行李提得很遠。每個火車站和旅館都有搬運工在等著，付一點小費就樂意幫你提行李。後來搭飛機的人數快速成長、機場變得非常大，旅客只好自己把隨身家當拖過走不完的走廊，情況才改變。面子可能也有影響。我的祖父因為工作經常出差，他覺得滾輪行李看起來很蠢，一直用手提著沉重的皮箱，直到背痛終於逼他讓步。也許一旦某個問題成了日常生活的一部分，我們就不再注意到它。每次我把行李箱推上火車，都很感謝終於有人想到了這個點子。
